what: Conditional Standard Error of Measurement in Generalizability Theory
title: Conditional Standard Error of Measurement in Generalizability Theory
text: goal csemGT estimate conditional standard error measurement (CSEM) within Generalizability Theory framework univariate, single-facet, persons--items (p × ) crossed design, following Brennan (1998). created maintained René Gempp, paralleling Stata module gtcsem. Unlike psychometric frameworks, Generalizability Theory distinguishes two types conditional measurement error: absolute CSEM, appropriate decisions concern absolute magnitude person’s score (example, mastery classification fixed cutpoint), relative CSEM, appropriate decisions concern comparisons among persons (example, ranking selection). csemGT estimates .

what: csemGT: Conditional Standard Errors of Measurement in Generalizability Theory — csemGT-package
title: csemGT: Conditional Standard Errors of Measurement in Generalizability Theory — csemGT-package
text: Estimates conditional standard error measurement (CSEM) within Generalizability Theory framework univariate, single-facet, persons--items (p x ) crossed design (Brennan, 1998). Returns person-level CSEM estimates absolute relative error variances, three estimators relative error variance (`full`, `large_a`, `uncorrelated`), closed-form analytical item-resampling bootstrap sampling variances, quadratic smoothing CSEMs observed score, D-study extrapolation.

Users `csemGT` able migrate `csemR` via simple `library()` change: function signature returned `csem` object designed identical.

what: Conditional standard errors of measurement under Generalizability Theory — csem_gt
title: Conditional standard errors of measurement under Generalizability Theory — csem_gt
text: Estimates conditional standard errors measurement (CSEMs) univariate, single-facet, persons--items (p x ) crossed design following Brennan (1998). Returns absolute relative error variances, three estimators relative error variance, closed-form analytical sampling variances, optional item-resampling bootstrap, quadratic smoothing, D-study extrapolation.

title: Conditional standard errors of measurement under Generalizability Theory — csem_gt
code: csem_gt(   data,   method = c("full", "large_a", "uncorrelated"),   error_type = c("absolute", "relative"),   conditioning = "total",   n_items_D = NULL,   bootstrap = FALSE,   R = 1000L,   bootstrap_type = c("item", "person"),   ci_method = c("percentile", "basic", "normal", "bca"),   ci_level = 0.95,   seed = NULL,   return_analytical = TRUE,   smoother = c("polynomial", "none"),   smoother_args = list(degree = 2),   exclude_extremes = FALSE,   cutpoint = NULL,   truncate_vc = FALSE,   truncate_negative_error_var = FALSE,   boot_keep_replicates = FALSE,   na_action = c("listwise", "fail", "pairwise"),   verbose = FALSE,   ... )

title: Conditional standard errors of measurement under Generalizability Theory — csem_gt
text: data Matrix data.frame, N persons J items, numeric complete (single-facet crossed design requires balanced data). method Character vector; one `"full"`, `"large_a"`, `"uncorrelated"`. Default: three. applies `error_type` includes `"relative"`. error_type Character vector; one `"absolute"`, `"relative"`. Default: . conditioning Either `"total"` (per-person mean items, .e. `rowMeans(data)`) numeric vector length N specifying alternative conditioning variable. Default: `"total"`. csemGT v1.0 `observed_score` `conditioning_value` coincide. n_items_D Integer; number items D-study extrapolation. Default: number observed items `data`. bootstrap Logical; `TRUE`, resampling bootstrap run. Default: `FALSE`. R Integer; number bootstrap replications. Default: 1000. bootstrap_type One `"item"` (default) `"person"`. item bootstrap default following Brennan (1998) matches `gtcsem` Stata package. ci_method One `"percentile"`, `"basic"`, `"normal"`, `"bca"`. Default: `"percentile"`. csemGT v1.0 confidence intervals Wald (normal-approximation) intervals; replicate-based methods deferred later release, non-`"normal"` request satisfied normal interval (requested effective methods recorded). ci_level Confidence level. Default: 0.95. seed Integer `NULL`; seed bootstrap. bootstrap engines restore prior RNG state exit, non-`NULL` seed leak caller's session. return_analytical Logical; `TRUE` (default), analytical SEs computed even `bootstrap = TRUE`. smoother One `"polynomial"` (default) `"none"`. smoother_args List smoother arguments. Default: `list(degree = 2)`. exclude_extremes Logical; `TRUE`, floor ceiling cases excluded smoother fit (unsmoothed CSEMs remain, `smoothed_csem.*` values `NA`). Default: `FALSE`. cutpoint Numeric `NULL`; cutpoint lambda mastery dependability coefficient Phi(lambda), mean-per-item scale `observed_score`. Default: `NULL` (computed). truncate_vc Logical; truncate negative ANOVA variance components zero. Default: `FALSE`. truncate_negative_error_var Logical; truncate negative per-person error variances zero taking CSEM square root. Default: `FALSE`. boot_keep_replicates Logical; retain bootstrap replicate summary output. Default: `FALSE`. na_action One `"listwise"` (default) `"fail"`. `"pairwise"` supported GT paradigm. verbose Logical; emit progress messages bootstrap. ... Reserved forward compatibility; currently ignored.

title: Conditional standard errors of measurement under Generalizability Theory — csem_gt
text: object class `csem`. Key components: `estimates` Data frame, one row per person, wide format.       Identifier columns `person_id`, `observed_score`,       `conditioning_value`, `group_size`, `extreme`, followed       `cov_xim` estimation columns `csem.<estimator>`,       `csem_var.<estimator>`, `se.analytic.<estimator>` /       `se.boot.<estimator>`, `ci_low.*` / `ci_up.*`,       `smoothed_csem.<estimator>`. `by_score` Data frame, one row per distinct observed score,       score-level summary estimation columns. `variance_components` ANOVA table, three variance       components, population-level error variances/SEMs,       reliability-like coefficients (`erho2`, `phi`, `phi_lambda`). `smooth_fits` Per-estimator smoother diagnostics, `NULL`       `smoother = "none"`. `bootstrap` Bootstrap metadata, `NULL`       `bootstrap = FALSE`. See [`new_csem`] full structure.

text: Scale. bootstrap engines return `per_person_variance` ERROR-VARIANCE scale (sampling variance \(\hat V_p\)). helper converts CSEM scale via delta method   \(\mathrm{Var}(\sqrt{V}) \approx \mathrm{Var}(V) / (4 V)\), using per-person point estimate `csem` (\(\sqrt{V_p}\)) evaluation point. result `csem_var.boot` therefore CSEM scale, dimensionally consistent `se.analytic` `.gt_add_analytical_se()` Wald intervals built `.gt_add_ci()`. Rows `csem <= 0` (NA) receive NA, since delta-method denominator defined . helper performs SE attachment . Confidence intervals attached separately `.gt_add_ci()` (spec v4 §5.3, steps 8 9).

title: csemGT 1.0.0
text: csem_gt() implements three relative-error estimators Brennan (1998) — full, large_a, uncorrelated — together closed-form absolute error variance (Brennan 1998, eq. 20). Closed-form analytical sampling variances item-resampling bootstrap variances four estimators. Quadratic smoothing conditional error variances observed score, optional exclusion floor ceiling cases. D-study extrapolation via n_items_D. S3 class csem full method set: print, summary, plot, .data.frame, by_score, coef. iowa_like synthetic dataset calibrated ITED Vocabulary Test. Two vignettes: tutorial introduction replication four published examples. Note: package first planned series. broader csemR package (development) integrate csem_gt() additional estimator families.
